# DuckLink core in the browser

Runs the same `ducklink_core.wasm` wasip2 component that `ducklink` runs
under `wasmtime`, in a browser (or any JS runtime with WebAssembly JSPI).

**JS bindings** — generated by
[`wit-js-bindgen`](https://github.com/tegmentum/wit-js-bindgen) from the
canonical WIT tree at `wit/core/wit` (the same tool elena-wasm uses for
its `@wasmos/protocol` bindings and its `@wasmos/dataset-ducklink`
provider). The generated `bindings/libduckdb.mjs` +
`bindings/libduckdb.d.mts` carry the WIT-derived TypeScript types plus a
self-contained `instantiate(module, imports)` factory (canonical-ABI
marshal + `WebAssembly.instantiate` on a core module).

**WASI runtime** —
[`@tegmentum/wasi-polyfill`](https://github.com/tegmentum/wasi-polyfill)
provides the WASI 0.2 plugin set the core imports (cli / io /
filesystem / clocks / random / sockets), and its `RuntimeBindgen`
handles the wasip2-component-to-core-modules unbundle step (invoking
`@bytecodealliance/jco/component` under the hood — a transitive dep of
wasi-polyfill, no longer a direct dep of this package). The custom
`duckdb:*` host imports (extension loader hooks, callback dispatch) are
stubbed for plain queries and rewired by `extension-host.mjs` when an
extension is loaded.

Why the migration off jco as a direct dep: elena-wasm and DuckLink both
share `wit-js-bindgen` as the canonical WIT-to-JS/TS generator (the
Tegmentum wasm ecosystem's uniform binding toolchain). Keeping jco as a
direct dep here duplicated the binding path; the migration keeps
`wit-js-bindgen` as the source of truth and lets wasi-polyfill own the
runtime transpile.

## What's here

- `bindings/` — `wit-js-bindgen` output for the `libduckdb` world.
  Regenerate with `npm run generate` (see below).
- `generate.sh` — thin wrapper around the `wit-js-bindgen` binary at
  `~/git/wit-js-bindgen/target/release/wit-js-bindgen`. Overridable via
  `WIT_JS_BINDGEN` / `DUCKLINK_WIT_DIR`.
- `run-core.mjs` — `configurePolyfill()` registers every WASI plugin the
  core imports; `runQuery(bytes, sql)` instantiates the core via the
  polyfill's `RuntimeBindgen` and runs a query. The generated bindings
  are imported for their TypeScript type surface (via JSDoc `@typedef`);
  the runtime instantiation still uses `RuntimeBindgen` because the
  component's core-module unbundle needs jco's `js-component-bindgen`
  under the hood.
- `browser-entry.mjs` + `index.html` — fetch the core wasm and show the
  result.
- `extension-host.mjs` — the extension-loading path (`verify-ext`).
- `tvm-host.mjs` — the TVM (spill) host that backs DuckDB's
  larger-than-memory sort.

```bash
npm install
# copy the core wasm next to index.html so the page can fetch it:
cp ../target/wasm32-wasip2/release/ducklink_core.wasm .
```

## Regenerate the JS bindings

Prerequisite: the `wit-js-bindgen` binary. Clone the sibling checkout
and build once:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tegmentum/wit-js-bindgen ~/git/wit-js-bindgen
(cd ~/git/wit-js-bindgen && cargo build --release)
```

Then, from this directory:

```bash
npm run generate    # regenerate bindings/libduckdb.mjs + .d.mts
```

Overrides:

- `WIT_JS_BINDGEN=/other/path/wit-js-bindgen npm run generate`
- `DUCKLINK_WIT_DIR=/other/wit/core/wit npm run generate`

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # vite dev server; open the URL and watch the <pre> fill in
npm run verify   # headless Chromium: instantiates + runs a query, prints result
```

`npm run verify` prints:

```
=== RESULT status: ok ===
columns: answer, two
rows: [[{"tag":"int64","val":"42n"},{"tag":"int64","val":"2n"}]]
```

i.e. `SELECT 42 AS answer, 1 + 1 AS two` ran inside headless Chromium —
DuckDB executing real SQL in the browser via the wasip2 component +
wasi-polyfill, no native host. (Values come back as WIT `duckvalue`
variants; the core renders them as text.)

## Known blocker: wasm exception-refs

Chromium probes today may fail inside jco's `js-component-bindgen`
transpile step with:

```
exception refs not supported without the exception handling feature (at offset 0x2cbd)
```

`ducklink_core.wasm` is built with `wasi-sdk 33`'s wasm
exception-handling proposal on (see this repo's top-level `README.md`:
"exception handling requires >= 33"). The shipped
`@bytecodealliance/jco@1.27.0` / `jco-transpile@0.6.3` don't enable that
wasm feature by default when their embedded `js-component-bindgen`
unbundles the component. Unblocks with one of:

1. A `jco` version bump that enables exception-refs by default in its
   embedded `js-component-bindgen`.
2. An upstream extension to `@tegmentum/wasi-polyfill`'s `jcoOptions`
   shape to plumb a `features` toggle through to
   `js-component-bindgen`'s transpile.
3. Rebuilding `ducklink_core.wasm` without exception handling —
   `-fno-exceptions` at the wasi-sdk / clang invocation site. DuckDB's
   C++ code uses exceptions extensively for error handling; going this
   route needs a broader audit than this landing carries.

Elena-wasm's `PLAN.md §14.21` (the shipped `@wasmos/dataset-ducklink`
landing note) captures the downstream state — the elena-wasm dashboard
demo boots this same component and hits the same failure at the same
transpile step; both consumers unblock together with any of the three
fixes above.

## Why the vite config looks the way it does

`vite.config.js` does two non-default things:

- `optimizeDeps.exclude` for `@tegmentum/wasi-polyfill` and
  `@bytecodealliance/jco` — wasi-polyfill's `RuntimeBindgen` dynamically
  imports the browser build of jco's `js-component-bindgen`
  (`js-component-bindgen-component.js`), which has a runtime-only
  `const offset = …; offset = …` reassignment that vite's esbuild
  pre-bundler rejects *statically*. Serving both packages as native ESM
  keeps that branch out of the pre-bundler.
- `server.fs.strict: false` — jco loads its own `.core.wasm` helpers
  from the linked `wasi-polyfill` checkout, which is outside the
  project root.

(The same `blob:` import jco uses under the hood is why this runs in
browsers but not Node's ESM loader — `run-core.mjs` run directly under
Node reaches transpilation then stops on `import(blob:)`.)

## Extension loading in the browser (working)

`npm run verify-ext` loads the **sample extension component** into the
in-browser DuckDB and calls its registered functions — the full
pipeline the native host drives, in the browser:

```
=== RESULT status: ok ===
scalar      sample_plus_one(41)        = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"42n"}]]
macro       sample_add_two(40)         = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"42n"}]]
cast        id-7 -> sample_id          = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"7n"}]]
logical     7::sample_id               = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"7n"}]]
table       sample_emit_sequence(4)    = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"0n"}],...]
aggregate   sample_sum(1..4)           = [[{"tag":"int64","val":"10n"}]]
replacement FROM 'hello.sample'        = [[{"tag":"text","val":"hello.sample"}]]
```

That is every capability the sample extension registers — scalar /
table / aggregate / cast dispatch back to the loaded extension
instance, while macro and logical-type run as core SQL — all in the
browser.

`extension-host.mjs` implements the host surface in JS:

- it instantiates the extension *component* (a second component
  transpiled through the same wasi-polyfill path) with JS
  implementations of `duckdb:extension/{runtime,catalog,files}` — the
  registry/callback resource classes capture what `load()` registers;
- it provides the *core's* `duckdb:component/{host-extension-loader,
  extension-loader-hooks}` + `duckdb:extension/callback-dispatch`
  imports, so the core sees the captured registrations and dispatches
  scalar/table/aggregate/cast callbacks straight back to the extension
  instance.

Because component instantiation is async but the core calls
`request-load` synchronously, extensions are **pre-loaded**;
`request-load` then returns the cached result and callbacks dispatch
synchronously.

## Consuming DuckLink from other JS packages

The elena-wasm workspace ships
[`@wasmos/dataset-ducklink`](https://github.com/tegmentum/elena-wasm/tree/main/packages/dataset-ducklink)
— a browser-side [`@wasmos/dataset`](https://github.com/tegmentum/elena-wasm/tree/main/packages/dataset)
provider backed by this exact `ducklink_core.wasm` binary. It's the
canonical wasmos-integration path: `createDuckLinkDataset({ corePath?,
sqlSeed?, ... })` returns a `Dataset` handle whose `query` / `subscribe`
/ `apply` verbs adapt `duckdb:component/database` to elena-wasm's
`wasmos:dataset` interface.

See [`../wasmos/README.md`](../wasmos/README.md) for the full
integration story.
